paragraphs: Ugh, in short, folks, I said … knows when — a couple of weeks ago or a little less — that “this week I'll show what I've been building all these months,” but I still haven't done it.
I think people who've actually vibe-coded something serious understand:

a) The emotion: it's unclear at what moment it's time to show, when 1,700 commits a month on a repo isn't the ceiling for you, meaning YOU MAKE 50+ COMMITS A DAY, and every commit is some substantial change (otherwise you wouldn't have requested it), which means the Strugatsky rule from “Hard to Be a God” applies:
“An hour is worth a life, and a day is priceless”
(Although most people probably know that line from Mnogotochie, or rather their feature with 25/17 =)
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=XiUiH0Bfazo&list=RDXiUiH0Bfazo&start_radio=1
I adore this track, what a philosophy those guys gave us, … me. I owe EVERYTHING in life to the crowd around Mnogotochie.)
b) I don't know how universal a trait this is, but there's no person in the world less confident in the … of what I've already built than I am, until it blows my own imagination.
However, what I've built blows my imagination every second day if not every first, but… the vision isn't 100% implemented yet. I'd even say I need 146% to calm down.
So you understand: when I ask Codex or PRO to analyze the current state of the repo, I ask for an assessment across every possible vertical against 10/10 and against 11/10.
10/10 is what we require. And 11/10 is what we actually need.

Then, by mechanics known only to me, I decipher the answer, and that answer is far more useful to me than if the LLM kissed my ass and said we're already at 10/10 after 600 commits spent polishing a single unit of front end.
However, today I had a get-together to which two guys came who vibe-code a lot.

Or rather: one vibe-codes a lot, and the second vibe-codes all the time, because it's his job. And the clients who buy the products of his vibe-coding are the best startups in the world and a fair number of British-American enterprises.

These were the first people in the world to whom I showed my entire whole system. Not fully, of course, because you can't see or tell in 15 minutes everything that happens on my back end. For 15 minutes I showed and explained only the front part, clicking buttons and briefly explaining what they were seeing.

It was cool and pleasant to watch the emotions of people who understand what they're being shown, and who ask questions at an accelerating pace as it dawns on them that this isn't a knock-off on someone's knee but a combat system already really working today on real clients, which in fact generates dough and in fact does the work of dozens of people who previously had to press all these buttons rather synchronously to deliver any result at all. “Any at all” matters, because even before thinking about quality, agency work is a very operational thing, and even if you don't think about quality at all — say, imagine something extremely …, templated, checked by nobody. To deliver simply anything at all in our niche, you have to press an awful lot of buttons.

And the guys saw for themselves that not only do I no longer need to press any buttons, but the quality this automated system produces is shocking in its wholeness and inventiveness, for a system nobody looks into and nobody clicks.
Just the day before yesterday I was celebrating another huge victory: I finally finished, to full 200% fail-proofness, a piece of the system that does the following:
ON ONE CLICK OF ONE BUTTON:
1) Check whether there's an uploaded video/audio with info about the business AND/OR the domain of the product we're going to sell
2) If not — request that content. If yes, is there already a result of the 5-stage market research

3) If not — run the research. If yes, from 20+ parameters of the research determine which domains, and how many, to correctly register for the given monthly campaign budget according to the domain registration methodology, and check their availability. When we've found, say, 100 domains, we try to register them on Porkbun. If some domains can't be registered on Porkbun — we go register the rest on Dynadot. If some can't be registered there — we go to the Cloudflare registry. The chain of connected registrars is such that it's hard to imagine a situation where the needed number of domains can't be registered, even if there are thousands of them, in one click.
4) Configure all domains perfectly for the task, push the needed DNS into Cloudflare.

5) Spin up, in our own ecosystem, 400 mailboxes for 100 domains (or any number of mailboxes for any number of domains within the rules, but I showed this example), and check that SPF/DMARC/DKIM/etc. (16 parameters) are configured perfectly, and that after all tests there isn't the slightest doubt that even one parameter differs from the reference (5 checks in a row to completely destroy any probability that even one domain dies from misconfiguration).

6) Put the mailboxes on the AI warm-up that I MYSELF created, which writes — I'm ready to bet my liver, kidneys and every pixel of my privates — the best emails by the most hardcore warm-up-correspondence mechanics in nature. All exclusively on AI, meaning not a single triggered action or text — absolute uniqueness across billions, even trillions of warm-up texts.
7) Launch another few dozen iterations of research to prepare the first test campaigns for work.
8) After a day of warming up the new mailboxes on the new domains — a celebration report on how perfectly everything listed went.
*If anything in the process isn't perfect, separate Codex instances are invoked via hook with the right prompting, and fix the process, relaunching it from scratch until it succeeds.
All of this happens on the click of ONE button in an interface that has … of buttons.
There are hundreds of such implemented flows, and most of them are hard to distinguish from magic in the complexity of what results from pressing one button.
Watching the faces of the guys I showed this to gave me confidence, because they couldn't hide how … they were long before the end of the presentation, and that was especially pleasant.
I put my soul, heart, body and all my time down to the second this year into this ….

Every time you saw me … around somewhere with the dog, at home a 4-session development was prepared and building without me, but as many experienced guys understand, it had to be prepared, and on that front, especially across many sessions, you can't win any time yet. I'm literally earning myself the time to leave the house these days. And even having left the house, I keep … two sessions into the watch — into the Telegram-bound headless Claude and Codex, separate from the main development in the apps on the computer.

In the end — the guy who, unlike me, makes money vibe-coding and developing for clients — choked on his gin and tonic when I told him the current system we were looking at has been written since March 23, 2026.

He of course immediately explained it to himself by the fact that I'd started from scratch several times before and gotten my hand in. In the same direction, that matters, but still he never understood how since March 23 I'd managed to … as much as I showed.

The dudes scratched their heads and said they've been in production IT all their lives, and what they saw is the level not of a junior, not a middle, not a senior coder, but of some senior architect with a not-…-small team under him, and a customer who understands very well what he needs, with very big experience in managing development — and even then they very much doubt that any senior-level person with a team of any size of meatbags could collectively have done everything they saw, even if nobody there ever went to sleep and they took turns shooting adrenaline and snorting amphetamines so as not to lose heart for a second.

That feedback inspired me to actually really show what … I've built. Now I'll look for the nearest day when healthy sleep coincides with a reduced number of Zoom calls and no theaters to attend, and … a stream where I'll show you the same thing I showed the guys offline today, only with another hundred or two commits on top;)

Over the past month more than ten people from the most varied worlds have DM'd me quite resonant warnings.

How their lid blew off in the process of excessive infatuation with vibe-coding, and they broke, lost companies, relationships, friends, partners, children, wives, money. Many note the appearance of uncontrollable delusions of grandeur, partial or complete loss of the ability to sleep normally, terrible nervousness, assorted symptoms at the physical level. These are things people don't write about publicly on their Facebooks, but out of kindness they type privately in DMs to those who might be at risk.

Sport and sex disappear from people's lives, the leaning on any bad habits increases, depression thickens with every day, which seems to bleach the meaning out of both what the person is vibe-coding and the hypothetical giving up of vibe-coding. The person ends up as if suspended in an uncertainty briskly filling with black emotions, and as that reservoir fills, in an ever more exhausted and haggard body, every day it gets harder to breathe.
I sort of understand what all these people are telling me, and I've felt every symptom they list on myself. And felt some individual ones of my own.

But this AI ailment won't take me so easily. Not that I consider myself better than those who broke. That's not it at all. Although I honestly admit to you that I sincerely believe I really am good. Otherwise I wouldn't be so disgusted when people kiss my ass. You see, it's hard to give a sufficient compliment to a person who knows how to praise himself alone, looking at his own reflection on the wall =) Oh, and here comes the symptomatology — delusions of grandeur in plain sight!
However, I have a defense more reliable than that.
I have a soft ….

A hard … harms everyone around, starting with the one who radiates it. Such people don't … care about others, which means they don't … care about themselves, because we're incapable of perceiving other people separately from ourselves. We look at people but see in them only what we're able to see — ourselves in each of them. If we could see them somehow differently, we would change, because one inevitably drags the other along. And we do change with experience and see others differently, but it's a long process. It owns us no less than we own it.

A soft …, on the other hand, is a useful component in battle. It has a mass of downsides, like everything in this vibrating world oscillating between good and evil. But it has a colossal draining effect on the psyche, the nervous system. A soft … is the ability to sincerely throw anything at all out of your head so it doesn't overflow. The … is soft only when it helps you live, not drown with a proud ….

Life is a heavy thing, and over time more and more and more diverse elements get thrown into our little cart, elements that have weight, and in sum it's heaviness. Don't forget physics: heavy things press down if you don't let them out of your head.

So, a soft … is when you don't forget your own Agents.md, in which the key principles are written, the saved memory of tasks and goals, the operating principles of things understood, and much, much more. Somewhere in there are skills too, and everything the subconscious sees fit to keep in RAM. Our Agents.md is of course colossal in size compared to what the poor AI of May 2026 can hold. You keep everything you need to keep in Agents.md, but the trick is not to keep everything else there.
Everything else you accept easily, tick the acceptance boxes, and just as easily let go. To … with it. Don't give a … at all.

Well yes, you have to strain the little head. Well yes, you have to constantly catch false joys followed by ten hours of clenched teeth. Well yes, sometimes you overstrained, didn't keep track, and the body gave up and … slept. Well yes, dropped out of life for a couple of weeks, or a month, or half a year. Well yes, … some options. Well yes, dug in your heels over some …, didn't listen to family and loved ones; they don't always have enough strength to put up with it. Well yes..

And if not all this, is life one solid gingerbread house or what? As long as I can remember, life has been one continuous problem. And as long as I can remember, life has been one continuous happiness. Many little problems and much little happiness. Relatives will get cancer, someone will even die. But you'll call the ones who are alive and you'll laugh, or meet and eat together, looking at each other with love and calm comfort.

Coming home, the dog brings enormous happiness with it. The dog brings enormous pain when it's sick, and costs to boot. The dog comes, looks at you, jumps on the couch and looks at you with loving eyes; you're under a blanket with tea, watching a great show. You're happy. Then the dog will die. You'll die too, but before that you have to process all this heartbreaking joy and all this terrible suffering.

Everything that has a beginning has an end. Absolutely everything will end. Looking back, I remember so much that was important but ended, and that I even managed to completely forget. Relationships, people, projects, jobs, grandmothers helped across the road, other people's run-over dogs nursed back to health, … and grateful clients, fights, bad trips, travels, and much, much, much, much, much more. Vibe-coding will end faster than the stretch of screeching modems and pagers. It's entertainment for two years at most. Most people won't even get to taste it, just as most people never heard the sound of a modem and never played Doom and Duke Nukem 3D.
And it feels as if before vibe-coding I lived somehow differently.

So, need to find employees. Need to find clients. Need to count the money. Damn, there's enough for a month and a half. Need to pay for the apartment. Need to pay for insurance. Rita decided to leave, took Anya and Dina with her. The guys are tearing their hair out; better they … looked for another Rita, … it, or did one of the thousand other useful tasks everyone knows about as well as I do, but until you ask, … nobody will strain themselves. Some … in the wing — needs fixing. Damn, two weeks of money left, but enough for payroll, so we haven't fallen that low. What next? Call, call, call, a hundred messages, human chaos. Money for a month and a half again. What does Marina want? A raise? Go … yourself, Marina. Tolyan, talk. Uh-huh, you saw problems. Of course you found … problems… I know, you can't even imagine, Tolya, how many there are besides the ones you see. Okay, you take this one and I'll take the rest, call when you've solved it. Or don't call; honestly I don't … care what you do, as long as you're doing at least something.
Want a chocolate bar. Bought a chocolate bar. …! When did I last play Dota? Well, hopefully I'll play once more this month. What's going on in the bank, let's go look? Those … still haven't paid, … .
Or say I had no business. Then THE SAME THING, one …. I remember that too. Reach a hand to any shelf and grab any memory.

…, they assigned me to the wrong store of course, but at least it's DNS-shop, the dream. … I'll finally touch this Hewlett-Packard, maybe someone will even buy one this week and I can talk them into letting me help install the software, at least let me touch this flawless touchpad, this fingerprint scanner… What … technology they've invented, …! Like the Strugatskys. Or even like Simmons! Have to be there at 8:30, an hour by minibus.
Hi guys, nice to meet you. What do you mean, did you see a pushover in me or what? Drop that, Vityok, or you and I will anti-befriend each other, got it, you … mutt …? That's right.

…, six people in the hall, where are the others? …, I'll serve everyone now. Yes yes Zina I'll drive those … documents in a sec, hold on, see, the guy over here might buy that very monitor right now, be a dear and show that girl the Sony Ericsson…
… of a day it was. What do you mean? What's an inventory count? So … we have two thousand SKUs. How-how many price tags to print???? AND STICK ON??!?!?? Okay then…

At 11:30 p.m. finished a bottle of beer with a shaking hand at the bus stop, thank God, the bus. Where are you going, Vityok? Let's go together, I'm one stop past you.. What, they say we have to be in at eight tomorrow? Well … eight it is. … we got lucky, bro, working in the trendiest store, in the ass end of it, true, but … what speakers, those red ones, huh? I'm …. The flash drive …? Look, …. … at the dumbass who …?!?! So he caught up with him after all, the rascal? Hahahaha well done)))

I don't see any difference. The day had 24 hours and still does. … has changed on that field. You can't be a child again. Life's not sugar? And why the … should it be sugar? Sugar is sugar, and life is life.

Recently went to the dentist after a 6-year break. Last was before COVID. And back then I'd dropped in on a dentist after a 13-year break. So the dentist says: how do you tolerate anesthesia? And I haven't the faintest …. Never, I say, had that stuff shot into me.
She goes, don't …, I can see you've got fillings. Well yes, but they did mine without anesthesia.
HOW?!

Well … I … know, just like that, don't they do it that way here? My doctor used to ask, should I inject anesthesia? And I'm a kid, the word “inject” sounds negative enough, easy to refuse, so I always refused. Why she drilled me like that, of course, is a separate question. But I have a great many questions for the most varied people from childhood, hardly many more than for the people who surrounded me at twenty, at thirty, or now. One …. What's the difference?

The doctor made sure I'd signed the paper saying no allergies, patient in full health, and shot me with anesthesia. All fine. Feel that? … I don't feel it. She fixes my teeth, I stare at the ceiling, thinking about some … of mine. She goes, …, maybe you're tired? How much more? … more? Well, I say, go on then, what difference does it make whether I'm tired or not? In the end she herself got tired two teeth in. Next time, she says, how long should I book you for? Book me, I say, for the whole … jaw. You can't! And how much can you? Well, two hours tops, you won't sit through longer, nobody does. … my …, Christy, just fucking try me. When your teeth are being drilled you don't have to … anything, don't have to decide anything, don't have to look at what's happening in the bank, don't have to listen to any … nonsense from anyone. What rest can you compare it to? I've never once relaxed like that even … on a tropical beach, there I've got the phone in my hands, which means work. And here, anesthesia, clean, you lie there enjoying it while others work, and you only get better in the process.

I absolutely DON'T GIVE A …. And if I stop … so completely, then what? A wizard will fly in on a blue helicopter and show me a movie? Or what the … will happen? I'll end up in a fairy tale? I don't want a fairy tale. I want to stay in reality, which is maybe why I only drink beer, otherwise I'd have stuffed myself with pills like Tolya and croaked long ago with a twisted ….

But I don't want to die, I want to live and be happy, which is why I so completely …. Without that people's minds leak, I see it everywhere. Everyone's so … spiritual, correct to the point of vomiting. Remember, bro, when you're spiritual, you don't shout about it. Your lids are whistling, otherwise you'd be able to put the letters in the right order at any time of day or night. Compared to many things in life, that's an elementary task.
I simply want not to be useless crap. And not for anyone else — I try for my most beloved self.

And right at this very moment I just want to grab the nearest chunk of dough and build myself a glass office in the garden, put a little couch next to it, and then I'll be able to do whatever … I want in that glass office, and if my body wants to relax — I'll flop onto the couch and sleep sweetly, like at a country house. Falling asleep, I'll look at the grass, and better if a breeze blows on it so it rustles barely audibly.
I'll wake up and grab dough for something else. And then for something else. And then again, and again, and again.
And even if my lid blows, well, … that too, we'll handle the matter. On the diagram it's still no different from everything that was before and will be after.
It seems to me people can be divided into those ready to consciously give up until their last breath, and those exclusively after it.

You can never assert which category you'll end up in tomorrow, but nobody can take away your right to strive to match whichever category suits your taste from this, as they say, limited assortment. And having chosen — match it. This is the case where you can't sit on two chairs at once. You can't run around comparing yourself to the greats, saying how you agree with every word of theirs, and then, frightened by any rustle in the body and especially in the mind, immediately drop the reins and turn into a candy doll. Either one or the other. And once you've chosen, live like that; everything else is …. You're allowed everything, nobody has the right to judge, and everyone will judge anyway. What's the difference.

Everyone just getting into vibe-coding should grasp one small important thing:

Nobody gets anything right on the first try, except small insignificant pieces. And even in those there's something to fix. If you don't see what needs fixing there — you simply haven't looked long enough =)

There's nothing bad about that. It doesn't make vibe-coding useless. It's still more useful (faster + cheaper + more valuable in features and in the look & feel of the result +…) than coding by humanoids by approximately thirty … times.

The most popular pattern I encounter among people who criticize vibe-coding: either it's slowly taking away their job, startups, the position in society they're used to, and they loudly agonize over it, or they tried, it didn't work, and they ticked the box “this … will never work for me.”
On the latest feature (which of course consists of hundreds of features, otherwise everything would work the first time; elementary things GPT 5.5 does flawlessly) I've been laboring for two weeks.

Right now I'm rebuilding it from scratch for the sixth time. The biggest iteration took 54 hours of continuous coding on 5.5 Xhigh. And all of it had to be thrown in the trash, like the previous stubbier iterations.

These 2 weeks aren't lost time; they are the true cost of development. They helped me figure out from which side I need to approach the important coupling nodes, where I under-thought, under-designed, under-tried. Today I got a working prototype that already performs the function, and this iteration took me only 4 hours.

In vibe-coding, as I suppose in real coding, it's incorrect to say you built a complex feature in 4 hours if you built it on the eighteenth try. You have to count all 19 attempts, the time spent on them, and work on the mistakes so that in future you spend 16, 12, or even fewer than ten attempts on similar things. But it's unlikely to work on the first. Nothing complex of mine has ever worked on the first attempt.
The only question there is always — will you have to rewrite from scratch, or can what previously came out in non-working form be combed into shape without the risk of later drowning in ….

Asking GPT to rip out what was created is also a separate skill. If you simply ask it to cut out some feature entirely — it'll cut it out so that you can start the whole project from scratch — you'll never find the ends … where it was knotted together and then chopped with an axe.
The main human quality of a vibe-coder is the same as a writer's — stamina.

You'll progress, of course, and what won't work for someone at all today will work for me on the first attempt after thousands of hours of exercise. But that progress is blurred by the progressing level of tasks a vibe-coder sets for himself.

The complexity of the features I design grows disproportionately to the growth of my expertise. I aim for such things that before these tasks I'm always a pathetic idiot, and I know the solution will cost me a week of … teeth-grinding.
Accordingly, sitting down to “immerse yourself in vibe-coding” — clear your schedule, forget your daily routines, families, friends and everything you call quality time, and everything will work out.
Or wait until vibe-coding becomes so simple that any product of any of your IT creativity will cost zero, and … nobody will need it. You can do that too =)
Both roads lead to the park. It's just that down one you walk with dough in your pocket, and down the other you drink from a puddle.
Vibe-coding is a skill, a process continuing in time

When there's AGI you'll simply ask for what you need, and not even HOW but precisely what, and you'll get it. The skill won't be needed. If something doesn't require a skill, it no longer costs anything, loses meaning, in the human sense.
For example, you drive a car — that's driving
She's a better driver than him, and he's a better driver than it
But nobody calls riding a bus as a passenger “bus-riding”
You can't say “He rides the bus better than she does”
Or rather you can say it, but the orderlies don't approve

Right now vibe-coding is what, how, in what manner, by means of what, etc. — lots of questions = skill = one vibe-coder can be hundreds of times more in demand than another = it makes sense to talk about it
In short, brothers and sisters, I'm really on the home stretch with this beast of a development.
When I finish, the first thing I'll do right after is upgrade the chess so that it opens not in a separate window of the … TG app, but in the browser.
TG apps are a mistake of nature. They shouldn't exist)
